name: DIFC Data Protection Law 2020
publisher: Dubai International Financial Centre (summarised by AEGIS)
licenseNote: The DIFC Data Protection Law (DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020) and its regulations are published by the DIFC. AEGIS summarises the obligations by principle in original wording under its own identifiers and does not cite article numbers; the DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection's guidance determines the operative detail. Not legal advice.
description: Principle-level map of the DIFC data protection regime for organizations in the Dubai International Financial Centre: lawful basis, principles, controller and processor duties, data subject rights, security, breach notification, transfers and the obligations attached to automated decisions and high-risk processing.

controls.title: Scope and registration
controls.summary: The organization has determined that its processing falls under the DIFC regime, is registered with the Commissioner where required and has named its accountable person.

controls.title: Processing principles
controls.summary: Personal data is processed lawfully, fairly and transparently, for specified purposes, limited to what is needed, accurate, retained only as long as necessary and kept secure.

controls.title: Lawful basis and consent
controls.summary: Each processing activity rests on a lawful basis the law allows, and where consent is used it is freely given, specific, informed and withdrawable.

controls.title: Special categories
controls.summary: Data revealing health, beliefs, origin, biometrics or similar is processed only under a specific condition with heightened safeguards.

controls.title: Controller accountability and policies
controls.summary: The controller implements and can demonstrate appropriate measures, policies and training, and keeps records of processing.

controls.title: Processor contracts
controls.summary: Processors act only on documented instructions under a contract covering security, confidentiality, sub-processing, assistance and the return or deletion of data.

controls.title: Data protection officer
controls.summary: A data protection officer is appointed where the law requires one, for example for high-risk processing, and is reachable by the Commissioner and data subjects.

controls.title: Data protection impact assessment
controls.summary: High-risk processing, including systematic profiling, new technologies and large-scale special categories, is assessed in advance and the Commissioner consulted where residual risk stays high.

controls.title: Transparency to data subjects
controls.summary: People are told who processes their data, why, on what basis, who receives it, where it goes, how long it is kept and what rights they have.

controls.title: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection
controls.summary: Data subjects can exercise their rights, and requests are handled within the time the law sets.

controls.title: Automated decisions and profiling
controls.summary: A person is not subject to a decision with legal or similarly significant effect based solely on automated processing without safeguards, including the right to human intervention and to contest it.

controls.title: Security of processing
controls.summary: Technical and organizational measures proportionate to the risk protect personal data against unauthorised or unlawful processing, loss and damage.

controls.title: Breach notification
controls.summary: A breach that compromises confidentiality, security or privacy is notified to the Commissioner as soon as practicable, and to affected data subjects where the risk to them is high, with records kept of every breach.

controls.title: Transfers out of the DIFC
controls.summary: Personal data leaves the DIFC only to a jurisdiction with adequate protection or under safeguards the law allows, such as approved contractual clauses or binding corporate rules.

controls.title: Sharing with public authorities
controls.summary: Requests from public authorities for personal data are assessed and recorded, and data is shared only where the law permits and with the safeguards it requires.
